The cheapest watch is not always the cheapest watch to own.

Two examples of the same reference can be sitting in front of you.

One is $1,000 less.

Easy decision, right?

Not necessarily.

The cheaper watch may also come with an unknown service history, heavier bracelet wear, missing links, aggressive refinishing, replacement parts, weak documentation, or mechanical issues that were impossible to see in the listing photos.

That is why I do not think purchase price should be evaluated by itself when buying pre-owned.

The better question is:

What will this watch actually cost me to own in the condition I want it?

Sometimes paying more for the better example is the less expensive decision.

Sometimes it is not.

The point is to know what you are buying before the “deal” becomes an expense.

What condition issue would make you walk away from an otherwise great watch?
